title: Strict diagrams as modules on a small site
statement: Let $J$ be a small category and $\mathcal C$ a small site with a sheaf $\mathcal O$ of commutative rings. On the small category $\mathcal D=J^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal C$, take the Grothendieck topology generated by the families $\{(\mathrm{id}_j,V_i\to U):(j,V_i)\to(j,U)\}_i$ for coverings $\{V_i\to U\}_i$ of $\mathcal C$ (a sieve is a collection of arrows with fixed target closed under precomposition; a Grothendieck topology assigns covering sieves satisfying maximality, pullback stability and local character; a sheaf is a contravariant set-valued functor for which every matching family on a covering sieve has a unique amalgamation). The presheaf $\mathcal O_{\mathcal D}(j,U)=\mathcal O(U)$, with identity action in the $J$ direction, is a sheaf of rings. There are equivalences $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(J,\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C))$ and $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_{\mathcal D})\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(J,\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], sending a sheaf $F$ to the diagram $j\mapsto(U\mapsto F(j,U))$ and sending morphisms to their components; the module equivalence is additive and exact. For each $j\in J$, evaluation is the inverse-image functor of a morphism of topoi $e_j:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ (an adjoint pair $e_j^{-1}\dashv e_{j*}$ with $e_j^{-1}$ preserving finite limits). Its right adjoint, in the diagram description, is $(e_{j*}A)(k)=\prod_{\alpha:k\to j}A$, with structure maps induced by precomposition. We have $e_j^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathcal D}=\mathcal O$, and the induced inverse image on module sheaves (inverse image followed by extension of scalars along this ring identification) is exact evaluation.
